description: Per ADR-025. Curated Delphi RTL → .NET / Java type mappings. Shipped as in-prompt context for every Delphi extraction call. v0 is intentionally small (~20 entries) to prove the shape; the full ~50-entry table per the ADR fills in during 9.0.b finalisation and as Indy extractions surface missing mappings.

semantics_notes: Delphi `string` is UnicodeString (UTF-16) in Delphi 2009+; AnsiString in 7-2007. Map to .NET string (UTF-16) and Java String (UTF-16) directly.

entries.dotnet_equivalent: System.String (caller transcodes from ANSI bytes if relevant)
semantics_notes: When the routine relies on the ANSI encoding (single-byte semantics), the translation MUST preserve that — typically by carrying a `byte[]` alongside the String. Flag as Open Question if the source isn't explicit.
Delphi Integer is 32-bit on Win32 + Win64. Map straight across.
Direct map.
Direct map. Note ByteBool / WordBool / LongBool are NOT equivalent (they're tri-state with non-zero = true); flag those separately.
Direct map. Caller is responsible for length tracking in both targets.

entries.dotnet_equivalent: System.Object (caller pattern-matches on the actual runtime type)
semantics_notes: Variant arithmetic coerces silently in Delphi (Variant + Variant returns the wider type). Java + .NET have no equivalent; a Variant-using routine almost always becomes an Open Question recommending explicit per-type handling.
TObject's `Free` method is the Delphi cleanup contract; in .NET this maps to IDisposable.Dispose, in Java to AutoCloseable.close.

entries.java_equivalent: java.lang.RuntimeException (or java.lang.Exception if checked semantics matter)
semantics_notes: Delphi exceptions are unchecked (all derive from Exception). The Java translation defaults to RuntimeException for parity; a Checked variant requires SME sign-off.
entries.ownership_model: RefCounted by the catch-block (the runtime owns the lifetime)
entries.thread_safety: Per-thread (raised + caught on the same thread).

entries.java_equivalent: java.io.InputStream / java.io.OutputStream (paired) OR java.nio.channels.ReadableByteChannel for random access
semantics_notes: TStream is bidirectional read/write/seek. .NET Stream matches directly. Java's InputStream + OutputStream split the read and write sides — the spec must surface which directions the routine uses so the archetype can pick.
Position / Seek maps to Stream.Position / Stream.Seek in .NET; to java.nio.channels.SeekableByteChannel in Java.
ByteBuffer is the closer match for random-access in-memory I/O; Byte{Input,Output}Stream for one-shot read or write.
Direct paired-readers/writers map.

entries.dotnet_equivalent: System.Collections.Specialized.NameValueCollection (for Names/Values use) OR System.Collections.Generic.List<string> (for plain ordered-string use)
entries.java_equivalent: java.util.LinkedHashMap<String, String> (for Names/Values use) OR java.util.ArrayList<String> (for plain ordered-string use)
semantics_notes: Routine that calls .Names[] or .Values[] needs the NameValueCollection / LinkedHashMap variant — flag the choice in the spec.
TStringList.Values[Name] empty-string-deletes (see edge-case rule); the .NET / Java translations DO NOT replicate that by default. Surface as Open Question.
Abstract base. Routines that accept `TStrings` (not `TStringList`) should be translated to take the interface, not the concrete class — `IList<string>` in .NET, `List<String>` in Java.

TThread.Execute → Thread.Start with a runnable. TThread.Terminated → CancellationToken / AtomicBoolean. TThread.Synchronize → SynchronizationContext.Post in .NET or SwingUtilities.invokeLater in Java. Note: .NET prefers Task/async; flag for SME decision.
entries.thread_safety: By definition cross-thread; flag for SME.

entries.dotnet_equivalent: System.ComponentModel.Component (legacy) OR a plain class (preferred for new code)
entries.java_equivalent: (no direct equivalent — translate to a POJO with an explicit owner ref)
semantics_notes: Delphi TComponent owns its sub-components and frees them in its destructor. The .NET / Java translations need an explicit owner-of-children pattern; flag as Open Question.

entries.dotnet_equivalent: (no direct equivalent — TPersistent supports streaming via RTTI which maps to System.Reflection patterns)
entries.java_equivalent: (no direct equivalent — translate to a POJO + a serialization library like Jackson)
semantics_notes: TPersistent's main feature is the streaming / RTTI machinery. Flag as Open Question with the suggested target serializer.

entries.dotnet_equivalent: (no direct equivalent — implements pattern is similar but reference counting is manual)
entries.java_equivalent: (no direct equivalent — Java has no ref-count contract on interfaces)
semantics_notes: IInterface gives ARC (automatic reference counting) on the object lifecycle. .NET and Java both rely on GC; explicit ARC wrappers are rare and usually unnecessary. The .NET translation typically uses IDisposable + a using-block at the consumption site; Java uses try-with-resources.
Reference cycles between IInterface refs cause leaks in Delphi. The GC-based targets don't leak (cycle collector handles them) but flag it as a side-effect for completeness.
entries.thread_safety: Increment/decrement is thread-safe in Delphi; the contained object is not necessarily thread-safe.

semantics_notes: Base implementation of IInterface ref-counting. The .NET / Java translation drops the ref-count machinery — GC handles it — but keeps the Disposable / Closeable contract for explicit-cleanup sites.
entries.thread_safety: Ref-count is thread-safe; object is not.

entries.dotnet_equivalent: System.Threading.Lock (System.Threading.Mutex for cross-process; lock keyword for in-process)
semantics_notes: TCriticalSection is in-process only. Map to `lock (obj) { ... }` in .NET; `synchronized (obj) { ... }` or ReentrantLock in Java. Acquire / Release map to lock.lock() / lock.unlock().
entries.thread_safety: By design — used to provide thread safety to other objects.

semantics_notes: Direct generic map.
entries.ownership_model: Owned (caller responsible for items unless using TObjectList<T>)

semantics_notes: TObjectList<T>.OwnsObjects is the distinguishing semantic. When OwnsObjects=true, the list frees children on Clear/Delete/destroy — the .NET target needs explicit Dispose() of items, Java relies on GC.
Flag OwnsObjects=true as a side-effect on the routine that adds items, so the SME sees the lifetime transfer.
Direct generic map. Note Delphi TDictionary doesn't preserve insertion order by default; if the source relies on order, the spec must call it out and the Java target should use LinkedHashMap.
